newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rosenthal raises capital to give Wedgwood a stake.
newsitem.headline: Rosenthal raises capital to give Wedgwood a stake.

text.p: German porcelain group Rosenthal AG said on Wednesday it planned to raise capital by 10 percent, saying this would enable Ireland's Waterford Wedgwood to take a stake in the group.
In a statement, Rosenthal said it had been seeking a strategic partner for some time and believed Dublin-based Waterford Wedgwood was an ideal choice.
"Waterford Wedgwood is the ideal partner to support Rosenthal's efforts to make greater progress in growth markets," the company said in a statement.
The capital increase, which would be proposed to shareholders for their approval at a meeting on January 31, would be made without rights being offered to current shareholders, Rosenthal said.
Shareholders would also be asked to approve plans to scrap a regulation capping the voting rights of shareholders in the company, the statement said.
The company's statutes currently allow individual shareholders to command a vote of no more than five percent, regardless of the number of shares actually held.
Rosenthal, which has a market capitalisation of just over 65 million marks ($42 million), did not specify whether Wedgwood would take all of the new shares issued in the capital rise.
Its shares closed unchanged at 108.50 marks on Wednesday. The market had already closed when the announcement was made.
